speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. Can you describe the event that immediately preceded your loss of consciousness, such as standing up quickly or being in a crowded room?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the syncope occurred right after urination, did you feel any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations in the moments before you passed out? Also, did you experience any dizziness or lightheadedness prior to the event?

REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram (ECG): No abnormalities. Echocardiogram: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis seems inconsistent with syncope occurring immediately after urination, which is often related to a vagal response rather than an infection. Did you notice any lightheadedness or a "warning" sensation right before you felt like you were going to pass out?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Urinalysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope (Cerebral Hypoperfusion). The clinical presentation of syncope immediately following urination, rapid recovery without confusion, and a normal workup strongly supports this benign vagal reflex, not a urinary tract infection.
